issues.legal_issue: A successor who was not in physical possession of claimed home-farm land when proprietary rights vested in the State cannot rely on the statutory preservation of possession to recover the land.
material_facts: A limited proprietor had created occupancy tenancy rights over some land before her death, and other land remained with her.
After the limited proprietor died, her husband took possession of the remaining land; the estate’s proprietary rights later vested in the State under the abolition legislation.
The plaintiffs succeeded to the estate but were not in physical possession of the disputed land on the date of vesting.
The plaintiffs sought possession of the disputed land as home-farm land.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiffs could not recover possession because they were not in physical possession of the land on the date of vesting; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 3 and 4(1) of the Madhya Pradesh Abolition of Proprietary Rights (Estates, Mahals, Alienated Lands) Act, 1950, proprietary rights vested in the State. Section 4(2), read with the definition of home-farm land in Section 2(g), preserved a proprietor’s ability to continue in possession of qualifying land only if already physically in possession; it did not confer a right to recover possession from another. The Court applied Haji Sk. Subhan v. Madhorao, which held that a person not in possession at vesting could not rely on Section 4(2) to continue to retain possession, and identified personal cultivation at the relevant times as central to the statutory scheme.

predicates.home_farm_possession_claim: The claimant brought a proceeding seeking possession of land claimed as home-farm land after proprietary rights in the estate vested in the State.
predicates.claimant_not_in_possession_at_vesting: The claimant was not in physical possession of the disputed land when the estate’s proprietary rights vested in the State.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks possession of land claimed as home-farm land after vesting and was not physically in possession at vesting, the claim to recover that land fails.
